body:
[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reverse_domain_name_notation) says:

> Reverse-DNS strings are based on registered domain names ... Reverse-DNS names are a simple way of eliminating namespace collisions, since any registered domain name is globally unique to its owner ...

This article references [flatpak's definition](https://docs.flatpak.org/en/latest/conventions.html#application-ids):

> The format is in reverse-DNS style, meaning the first section should be a domain controlled by the project

However I agree that it is very ambiguous, and not all definitions of reverse-DNS mention this. The convention suggestion just felt a little pointless if I didn't include this, which is why I added it in.
